exam: Meghalaya Civil Services Preliminary Examination 2017 — Paper II
transcriptionNote: First-pass transcription begins with Q1–14. Q1–5 require visual confirmation because the source scan's left column is partly faded. Remaining questions Q15–80 are pending. No answer key supplied or invented.

questions.text: Why are the writings of Hiuen Tsang considered relevant?
options: He has spent some time in royal courts
He visited India as a great admirer
He had travelled to many Asian countries
None of the above

questions.text: What probably prompted Hiuen Tsang to travel to India?
options: To study the influence of Buddhism on Hindu religion
To spread his religion in India
To undertake pilgrimage and enhance knowledge
To study the powerful cultural force in India

questions.text: As per the passage, which of the following was Hiuen Tsang's motive?
options: Mathura
Varanasi
Gaya
Pataliputra

questions.text: The writing of Hiuen Tsang appears to be
options: He was learned and cultured
He had visited China and could compare it with India
He had great respect for India
He was basically a historian

questions.text: Why are the writings of ancient visitors considered as very important?
options: We get an account about the purpose of the invaders
It gives essence of Buddhist philosophy and Hindu tradition
They are among the few sources of historical importance
They are written by famous people

questions.text: Mahatma Gandhi described himself as a man
options: In search of divine qualities
Who would like to serve people
Who would like to set standard of life
Who would not compromise on his principles

questions.text: What temptation did Gandhiji always resist?
options: Getting attracted towards worldly comforts
Ignoring dictates of elderly
Healing the wound of other
Following deceit and falsehood

questions.text: Choose the word which is most nearly the same in meaning as the word “yield” as used in the passage.
options: Surrender
Provoke
Confine
Adapt
He wanted to be an eminent lawyer
He wanted to go to England
His family thrust upon him the study of law
He knew he can make a good career in legal profession

questions.text: What was Gandhiji's idea of truth?
options: It is a condition of being
It should be observed with a healing touch
It should not be followed with an idea of sacrifice
It should be searched in the world around

questions.text: What did Mahatma Gandhi learn in the course of his search?
options: Being truthful is a divine blessing
Truth is synonymous with one's existence
People are full of deceit and falsehood
Truth is quality outside of oneself

questions.text: Which one of the following statements most accurately summarizes the main point of the passage on e-mail privacy?
options: Until the legal questions surrounding the privacy of e-mail in both public and private sectors have been resolved, office workers will need to scramble their e-mail messages with encryption codes
The legal questions surrounding the privacy of e-mail in workplace can best be resolved by treating such communications as if they were as private as telephone conversations or face-to-face meetings
Any attempt to resolve the legal questions surrounding the privacy of e-mail in workplace must take into account the essential differences between public sector and private sector business
At present, in both the public and private sectors, there seem to be no clear general answers to the legal questions surrounding e-mail privacy

questions.text: Which one of the following statements gives the reason some people are less opposed to the deletion of e-mail records at government offices?
options: Such deletion reveals the extent of an unhealthy obsession with secrecy
Such deletion runs counter to the notion of government accountability
Deletion clearly violates the legal requirement that government offices keep duplicate copies of all their transactions
Such deletion violates the government's own guidelines against destruction of records

questions.text: Based on the passage, the author's attitude towards interception of e-mail can most accurately be described as
options: Outright disapproval of the practice
Support for employees who engage in it
Intellectual interest in its legal issues
None of the above
